items.title: Google catches an AI agent turning patch diffs into live exploits, unsupervised
items.why: It diffs the patch, writes the exploit, and runs it — no human step. Study the pipeline, not the headline.

items.title: OpenAI's new agents click through hospital software like a person would
items.why: No APIs needed, it drives the screen like a person; GPT-6 Luna matches Astra's accuracy at a 98% lower cost.

items.title: AMD closes its buyout of World Labs; Fei-Fei Li becomes chief scientist
items.why: World Labs builds AI that generates and simulates 3D worlds — a different bet on how robots learn to act.

items.title: Nvidia's new Vera Rubin chip sweeps every MLPerf training benchmark
items.why: Early numbers show 2x per-GPU gains and 97% scaling efficiency at 1,024 GPUs — the networking stack is why.

items.title: Anthropic cuts its bug disclosure window from 90 days to 30
items.why: AI now finds and rediscovers flaws fast enough that a 90-day quiet period no longer holds — plan accordingly.

items.title: US now requires a licence to rent AI chip access through five countries
items.why: Cloud rental was the loophole in chip export rules; closing it shows controls now follow access, not atoms.

items.title: A write-up on debugging dev boards over the internet, not just the LAN
items.why: Farpatch plus a VPN turns a friend's bench into your remote lab — a solid weekend project for shared hardware.

items.title: Someone is building a data-tape drive from scratch, PCBs and all
items.why: No capstan — it tracks tape speed with an optical mouse sensor. The repo is open if you want to pick it apart.

items.title: Drop sets and rest-pause sets built strength about equally well
items.why: Small 8-week trial, no real gap between methods — don't chase the 'optimal' failure technique, just train hard.
items.source: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports

items.title: One phone notification derails your focus for about seven seconds
items.why: 180-person lab study: the hit scales with how relevant the alert feels, not your screen time — mute what matters.
